tomas.t: What both photos have in common is that people are working, and in both cases they seem quite focused.
Whereas the first photo shows a team in a formal meeting, the second one shows someone working on their own in a café.
Judging by their serious faces, the people in the meeting might be under much more pressure than the person in the café.
Mainly because they probably have to agree on an important decision before the meeting ends.
So I'd say the meeting is harder, although the noise in the café could make it difficult to concentrate.

beatriz.t: Both photos show people working.
In the first photo there's a meeting in an office, but in the second photo someone is working alone in a café.
Maybe the people in the meeting are stressed, because their boss is there.
Maybe the person in the café is tired, because it's very noisy.
I think working in the meeting is more difficult.

tomasFollow.t: That's a difficult one, but I'd rather work in the café.
I like being able to choose my own music and take a break whenever I want.
For example, when I study for tests, I often go to a café near the cathedral with my laptop.
However, I'd probably miss having other people around to help me.

beatrizFollow.t: Hmm, I'd prefer the café.
It looks more relaxing.
Mainly because I don't like long meetings.

tomas.t: Both photos show people surrounded by others, and neither place looks very private.
Whereas the first photo shows a crowded street at night, full of lights, the second one shows a group of students working quietly in a library.
From the way everyone is walking, the people in the street might feel more excited, but also more rushed, than the students.
The students, on the other hand, look as if they're helping each other, probably because they have an exam soon.
So I'd say the students feel calmer, even though they're probably a bit worried about their results.

beatriz.t: Both photos show a lot of people.
In the first photo the people are in a busy street, but in the second photo they are in a library.
Maybe the people in the street are happy, because it's the weekend.
Maybe the students are tired, because they're studying for an exam.
I think the people in the street feel more relaxed.

tomasFollow.t: Hmm, honestly, I'd rather be in the street.
I love places with lots of lights and music, like the centre of Funchal at Christmas.
Mainly because there's always something happening.
But the day before an exam, I'd definitely choose the library!

beatrizFollow.t: Oh, I'd rather be in the street!
It looks really fun at night.
Especially with my friends, after a long week at school.

tomas.t: What these photos have in common is that people are relaxing together, and in both cases they seem to be having a good time.
Whereas the first photo shows people watching a film in a cinema, the second one shows a family playing a board game at home.
The people in the cinema might have chosen a film because they wanted to escape from everyday life, whereas the family must have wanted to spend time together.
For example, while you're playing a board game, you can talk and laugh, which is impossible in a cinema.
So I'd say they both chose well, but the family probably had a much cheaper evening!

beatriz.t: Both photos show people having fun.
In the first photo people are at the cinema, but in the second photo a family is playing a game at home.
Maybe the people at the cinema chose a film because they wanted to relax.
Maybe the family chose a game because it's cheaper.
I think the family is having more fun.

tomasFollow.t: On a Saturday evening? Definitely the cinema.
My friends and I go to the cinema in the shopping centre about once a month.
Mainly because the big screen makes action films much more exciting.
However, when my cousins visit, we always end up playing board games until midnight.

beatrizFollow.t: Oh, I'd rather go to the cinema.
I love watching films on a big screen.
Especially action films, with my friends.

tomas.t: Both photos show places where people go shopping, and in both cases there seems to be a lot of choice.
Whereas the first photo shows a huge, modern shopping centre, the second one shows a traditional market with small stalls.
Judging by how busy it looks, shopping in the mall might be more convenient, but also more stressful, than shopping at the market.
For example, at the market you can probably talk to the sellers and taste the fruit before you buy it.
So I'd say the market is more enjoyable, although it could be frustrating if it starts to rain.

beatriz.t: Both photos show people shopping.
In the first photo there's a big shopping centre, but in the second photo there's a small market.
Maybe shopping in the mall is easy, because all the shops are together.
Maybe the market is more fun, because the food is fresh.
I think the mall can be frustrating when it's crowded.

tomasFollow.t: Where do I prefer to go shopping? It depends on what I'm buying.
For clothes I go to shopping centres, but for fruit I love the Mercado dos Lavradores.
Mainly because the fruit there is fresher and much tastier.
The only problem is that it's always full of tourists taking photos!

beatrizFollow.t: Hmm, I prefer shopping centres.
I usually go to the one near my house.
Mainly because there are lots of clothes shops.

tomas.t: What both photos have in common is that people are spending time in nature, and in both cases they seem to be far from the city.
Whereas the first photo shows a peaceful beach at sunset, the second one shows someone hiking in the mountains.
The people on the beach might have decided to relax after a long day, whereas the hiker must have wanted a much bigger challenge.
Judging by the hiker's heavy backpack, they've probably been walking for hours.
So I'd say they both wanted to escape from everyday life, but in very different ways.

beatriz.t: Both photos show people outside in nature.
In the first photo there's a beach at sunset, but in the second photo someone is walking in the mountains.
Maybe the people on the beach went there because they wanted to relax.
Maybe the hiker wanted to do some exercise.
I think the beach is more relaxing.

tomasFollow.t: That's an easy one for me: the mountains!
I often walk the levadas with my dad, and the views are incredible.
For example, last month we walked from Pico do Arieiro to Pico Ruivo.
Even though my legs hurt for two days, it was worth it.

beatrizFollow.t: Oh, I'd prefer the beach.
I love watching the sunset.
Especially in summer, when it's warm in the evening.

tomas.t: Both photos show people learning, and in both cases someone seems to be helping someone else.
Whereas the first photo shows students studying together in a library, the second one shows a parent helping young children with a tablet at home.
The students might be learning how to work as a team, while the children are probably learning something much simpler, like numbers or colours.
Judging by their smiles, the children seem to think it's a game.
So I'd say the students are learning more facts, but the children are learning to enjoy learning.

beatriz.t: Both photos show people learning.
In the first photo students are in a library, but in the second photo children are at home with a tablet.
Maybe the students are learning for an exam.
Maybe the children are learning numbers, because they are very young.
I think the children are having more fun.

tomasFollow.t: Easier to learn? Definitely with other people.
When I study with my friends, we explain things to each other.
For example, before our last history test, we met in the library and tested each other.
However, if my friends start talking about football, I learn nothing at all!

beatrizFollow.t: Hmm, I find it easier at home.
I study in my bedroom.
Mainly because it's quiet.

tomas.t: What these photos have in common is that people are doing exercise, and in both cases they look very determined.
Whereas the first photo shows a team playing football outdoors, the second one shows someone training alone in a gym.
The footballers might be developing teamwork and communication, whereas the person in the gym is probably developing more self-discipline.
Mainly because nobody is there to push them, so they have to motivate themselves.
So I'd say team sports develop social skills much more than training alone does.

beatriz.t: Both photos show people doing sport.
In the first photo a team is playing football, but in the second photo someone is training alone in a gym.
Maybe the football players are learning to work together.
Maybe the person in the gym is getting stronger.
I think football is better, because you can make friends.

tomasFollow.t: That's a good question! I'd rather play a team sport.
I've played football for a club since I was seven.
Mainly because I love the feeling when the whole team celebrates a goal.
Although training alone could make me stronger, I'd get bored very quickly.

beatrizFollow.t: I'd rather play a team sport.
I play volleyball at school.
Mainly because it's more fun with friends.

tomas.t: Both photos show people travelling, and in both cases they seem to be seeing something new.
Whereas the first photo shows tourists visiting famous buildings in a city, the second one shows someone on an adventure by a lake in the mountains.
Judging by their cameras, the tourists might remember the famous places they've seen, whereas the traveller is more likely to remember how they felt.
For example, sleeping in a tent next to a lake is something you never forget.
So I'd say the adventure is probably more memorable, although the city trip might be more comfortable.

beatriz.t: Both photos show people on holiday.
In the first photo tourists are in a city, but in the second photo someone is in the mountains.
Maybe the tourists will remember the famous buildings.
Maybe the person in the mountains will remember the beautiful lake.
I think the trip in the mountains is more memorable.

tomasFollow.t: Which kind of trip? Hmm, I'd enjoy the adventure more.
I prefer being outdoors to waiting in long queues for museums.
Mainly because I grew up surrounded by mountains and the sea.
But if my parents paid for a trip to New York, I wouldn't say no!

beatrizFollow.t: Oh, I'd enjoy the city trip more.
I love visiting famous places.
Especially museums and big shops.
